title: Multivariable Prediction of Hypotension during General Anesthesia using Preoperative Nocturnal Blood Pressure Data
summary:
Low blood pressure often occurs in people undergoing surgery under general anesthesia. Blood pressure that is too low can be associated after surgery with damage to the heart and kidneys and, in severe cases, with an increased risk of death. Blood pressure may drop either shortly after the start of anesthesia, before the operation begins, or during the operation itself.
It is difficult to predict which patients will experience a significant drop in blood pressure. This is because many factors play a role, such as how anesthesia is managed, how the surgery proceeds, and an individual’s overall health. A better understanding of these personal risk factors could help detect drops in blood pressure at an early stage or even prevent them. This could substantially reduce possible complications around the time of surgery.
Existing prediction models provide initial guidance but are not yet reliable enough. Therefore, in our study, additional measurements will be performed before surgery. These include, among others, nighttime blood pressure measurements and ultrasound examinations of the heart. The goal is to use this information to better assess the risk of blood pressure drops during and after the induction of anesthesia.

interventions.name: Preoperatively, non-invasive nocturnal blood pressure monitoring and transthoracic echocardiography are performed. Perioperatively, routinely collected vital parameters are monitored, with particular emphasis on dipping patterns.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Elective, non-cardiac surgery under general anesthesia
- Possession of health insurance
- Provision of written informed consent
- Presence of at least one cardiovascular risk factor (CVRF) and/or an established cardiovascular disease (CVD) in accordance with current guidelines
Exclusion criteria:
- Contraindications to 24-hour blood pressure monitoring
- Intensive care unit admission within the last 30 days
- Pregnancy or breastfeeding
